statement: A cheetah can run at a top speed of about $112$ kilometers per hour. What is this speed in meters per second, to the nearest tenth? ($1$ kilometer $= 1{,}000$ meters)

choices.misconception: I remembered that 3.6 links kilometers per hour to meters per second, but I multiplied 112 by 3.6 instead of dividing.
I changed kilometers to meters and divided by 60, which gives meters per minute, not meters per second.
I changed kilometers to meters but never changed hours to seconds, so I gave meters per hour.

hints: Change kilometers to meters and hours to seconds.
$112$ kilometers is $112{,}000$ meters, and $1$ hour is $60 \cdot 60 = 3{,}600$ seconds.

solutions.reliable: In one hour the cheetah would cover $112 \cdot 1{,}000 = 112{,}000$ meters, and one hour is $3{,}600$ seconds. So the speed is $112{,}000 \div 3{,}600 \approx 31.1$ meters per second.
solutions.elegant: Chain the units: $\frac{112 \text{ km}}{1 \text{ h}} \cdot \frac{1{,}000 \text{ m}}{1 \text{ km}} \cdot \frac{1 \text{ h}}{3{,}600 \text{ s}} \approx 31.1 \text{ m/s}$.

author: Devansh Sanghavi
